sources.dataset: World Urbanization Prospects 2025 Revision - Degree of Urbanization
sources.coverage: Annual population 1950-2050; land and built-up area 1975-2050
sources.unit: internationally harmonized cities, towns and semi-dense areas, and rural areas
sources.role: Primary statistical panel and national urbanization-stage controls
sources.citation: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2025). World Urbanization Prospects: The 2025 Revision, Online Edition.
sources.notes: The 2025 download center supersedes older WUP table numbering. Register the exact downloaded file rather than assuming legacy F-table names.

sources.unit: DEGURBA urban centre with multi-temporal footprints and attributes
sources.role: Spatial footprint, density, area-change, geometry and boundary sensitivity
sources.citation: European Commission, Joint Research Centre. GHS Urban Centre Database 2024, R2024A.
sources.notes: Do not describe as an independent replication of WUP 2025; both depend on the GHSL/DEGURBA system. Preserve dynamic and fixed-boundary analytical streams.

sources.role: National demographic controls and forecast baselines
sources.citation: United Nations, Department of Economic and Social Affairs, Population Division (2024). World Population Prospects 2024.
sources.notes: Use vintages available at each historical forecast origin when testing genuine real-time forecasts; the current revision is revised-history evidence.

sources.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
sources.dataset: OECD Cities and Functional Urban Areas
sources.coverage: OECD FUAs and worldwide estimated FUAs where published
sources.citation: OECD. Cities and Functional Urban Areas database.
sources.notes: Not globally interchangeable with GHSL urban centres; use on its supported sample as a mechanism test.

sources.citation: WorldPop, University of Southampton. Global high-resolution population estimates.
sources.notes: Top-down estimates are adjusted to national totals and are too short for the primary 1975-forward persistence analysis.
